questions.section: How an air-breathing engine makes thrust
questions.question: A jet engine flies at V∞ = 200 m/s with matched exit pressure (pe = p∞). Air enters at 50 kg/s, fuel enters at 1.0 kg/s, and exhaust leaves at Ve = 600 m/s. What thrust does the engine produce?
questions.explanation: With pe = p∞, T = (50 + 1.0) × 600 − 50 × 200 = 30,600 − 10,000 = 20,600 N = 20.6 kN. 30.6 kN omits the inlet ram drag (50 × 200); 20.0 kN leaves out the fuel mass flow; 40.6 kN adds inlet momentum instead of subtracting it.

questions.section: How an air-breathing engine makes thrust
questions.question: An engine cruises at V∞ = 250 m/s and discharges its exhaust at Ve = 750 m/s. What is its ideal propulsive efficiency ηp?
questions.explanation: Ideal propulsive efficiency is ηp = 2 / (1 + Ve/V∞) = 2 / (1 + 750/250) = 2/4 = 0.50, or 50%. 33% computes V∞/Ve; 67% computes 2/(750/250); 75% computes Ve/(Ve + V∞) = 750/1,000 instead of 2V∞/(Ve + V∞).

questions.section: How an air-breathing engine makes thrust
questions.question: To raise propulsive efficiency at a fixed cruise speed and fixed thrust, how should a propulsion designer change the air mass flow rate and exhaust velocity?
options: Move a larger mass flow rate of air through a smaller speed increase
Move a smaller mass flow rate of air at a much higher exhaust velocity
Raise both mass flow rate and exhaust velocity together
Lower mass flow rate while keeping exhaust velocity equal to flight speed
questions.explanation: Because ηp = 2/(1 + Ve/V∞), lowering Ve toward V∞ wastes less kinetic energy in the wake; keeping thrust T ≈ (air mass flow)(Ve − V∞) constant then requires a larger air mass flow rate. Setting Ve = V∞ gives zero thrust.

questions.section: Stages of a turbojet and the engine families
questions.question: In what order does air pass through the five main stages of a turbojet engine?
options: Inlet, compressor, combustor, turbine, nozzle
Inlet, turbine, combustor, compressor, nozzle
Inlet, combustor, compressor, turbine, nozzle
Compressor, inlet, turbine, combustor, nozzle
questions.explanation: Air enters the inlet (diffuser), is pressurized in the compressor, heated by burning fuel in the combustor, expanded across the turbine (which turns the compressor shaft), and accelerated out the nozzle.

questions.section: Stages of a turbojet and the engine families
questions.question: Where inside a turbojet do static pressure and static temperature reach their highest values?
options: Pressure peaks leaving the compressor; temperature peaks leaving the combustor
Both pressure and temperature peak leaving the nozzle
Both pressure and temperature peak leaving the compressor
Pressure peaks leaving the turbine; temperature peaks leaving the inlet
questions.explanation: The compressor raises pressure to its peak; the combustor burns fuel at nearly constant pressure to drive temperature to its peak; then both pressure and temperature drop through the turbine and nozzle.

questions.section: Stages of a turbojet and the engine families
questions.question: What is the primary role of the turbine in a pure turbojet engine?
options: Extract energy from the hot gas to spin the compressor through the connecting shaft
Accelerate the exhaust gas to supersonic speed to create thrust directly
Compress the incoming outside air before fuel is injected
Mix bypass air with core exhaust to lower jet noise
questions.explanation: The turbine extracts just enough energy from the combustor exit flow to turn the shaft that drives the compressor (and fan or propeller on other gas turbines). Accelerating the exhaust is the nozzle's job, compressing outside air is the compressor's job, and a pure turbojet has no bypass duct.

questions.section: Matching an engine to a mission
questions.question: Why does the propulsive efficiency of a propeller aircraft drop sharply once flight speed passes about Mach 0.55?
options: Forward speed plus blade rotation drives the propeller tips near Mach 1, causing shock losses
Air density becomes too low for any gas-turbine core to run
Propellers cannot produce thrust unless exhaust pressure exceeds ambient pressure
The reduction gearbox stops transmitting shaft torque above Mach 0.55
questions.explanation: The local flow speed at the spinning blade tips is the vector sum of forward speed and tip speed; past flight Mach 0.55 the tips enter transonic flow, shock waves form on the blades, and efficiency plunges. Gas-turbine cores run well above Mach 2.

questions.section: Matching an engine to a mission
questions.question: A new long-range airliner must cruise at Mach 0.82 across oceans while minimizing fuel burn and airport noise. Which engine family is the best choice?
options: High-bypass turbofan, because its large cool fan flow gives high propulsive efficiency and low TSFC at Mach 0.82
Turboprop, because propellers always have lower fuel burn than turbofans at every subsonic Mach number
Afterburning turbojet, because it has the highest specific thrust
Ramjet, because it removes the heavy compressor and turbine
questions.explanation: At Mach 0.82 a high-bypass turbofan avoids propeller tip shocks (its inlet slows air ahead of the fan) while moving a large mass flow at moderate exhaust speed for low TSFC and low noise. Turboprops lose efficiency past Mach 0.55; afterburning turbojets are loud and fuel-hungry; ramjets produce zero static thrust and need supersonic flight above Mach 2.
